Helena Buonanno Foulkes

Democratic candidate for Governor, Rhode Island · Open seat

Businesswoman; former president of CVS Pharmacy and former CEO of Hudson's Bay Company

Helena Buonanno Foulkes, 62, of Providence, is a former CVS Health executive and former CEO of Hudson's Bay Company. She ran for governor in 2022 and lost the Democratic primary to Gov. Dan McKee. In September 2026 she beat McKee in a rematch to win the Democratic nomination. She faces Republican Aaron Guckian and independent Ken Block on Nov. 3, 2026.

Where Foulkes stands

Housing
Proposes a 'Rhode Home' program that she says will create 20,000 homes and apartments people can afford by 2034, funded by a millionaire's tax and run as a low-interest loan program for developers.
Taxes
Supports a state millionaire's tax to pay for her housing program.
Health care
Supports raising Medicaid reimbursement rates and says the state should stop leaving federal money unused. She says this would help keep primary care doctors and nurses in Rhode Island.
Jobs and economy
Proposes $100 million for classroom-to-career programs and says she will remove barriers for businesses that want to stay, grow or start in the state.
State pensions (retiree COLAs)
Says she cannot commit to restoring retiree cost-of-living increases until she better understands what it would cost.
Education
Supports holding back third graders who are not proficient in reading, based on a model started in Mississippi.
Judicial selection
Supports having magistrate judges go through the same merit-based Judicial Nominating Commission review used for Superior and Supreme Court judges.
Sports betting
Said yes when asked whether the state should take another look at its sports betting laws because of addiction concerns, especially for young people.
Transparency / tax returns
Released summaries of her tax filings and has called on her opponents to release theirs.
Federal policy
Criticized Trump administration policies, including immigration enforcement, cuts to food assistance and Medicaid, and tax breaks for billionaires.
